title: Gesture-driven Rail Navigation — Console IA Prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current Console sidebar and workspace switcher are optimized for click/tap and dense menus but do not support fluid multi-touch gestures, quick peeks across workspaces, or gesture-primed route previews. Our customers building monitoring dashboards and rollout pages repeatedly ask for faster, less disruptive navigation flows so they can pivot between cost views, active rollouts, and model routes without losing context.

Goal: Prototype a gesture-driven rail navigation pattern (swipe/drag/edge-swipe + two-finger peek) that: 1) surfaces workspace context and active rollouts without a full context switch, 2) preserves deep-linking and route history for telemetry, and 3) exposes a lightweight cost-lens quickpeek tied to the current route. The prototype should validate discoverability, conflict-free gestures (with OS-level gestures), accessibility fallbacks, and integration points for rollout controls and cost breakdown badges.

Scope: Design interactive Figma prototype for desktop (trackpad) and tablet (touch), a short research script for 6 observational sessions, and a design spec for ENG and PM describing intents, telemetry hooks, rollout affordances, and progressive rollout strategy. Excludes full mobile native implementation (tracked separately).

Proposed solution (high level): Implement a compact left rail with three gesture zones: edge-swipe for workspace peek, central-rail drag for breadcrumbed route scrubbing, and pinch-on-rail to toggle cost-lens overlay. When a workspace peek is invoked, the rail expands into a translucent overlay showing top-level dashboards, active rollouts with status chips, and a play/pause quick action for canary rollouts. Deep click into the overlay performs a full workspace switch. The interaction should be keyboard-accessible (Alt/Cmd+← to peek) and provide explicit controls for users with reduced motion.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Prototype supports at least two gesture flows (edge-swipe peek, drag route scrub) on desktop trackpad and tablet touch within Figma interactive prototype.
- Usability: 6 research sessions show >80% task success (open rollout quick actions, reveal cost-lens, switch workspace) and fewer than 2 major errors per participant.
- Engineering spec includes telemetry hooks (peek_open, peek_close, cost_lens_open, route_scrub) and a safe default that disables gestures on legacy browser/OS combinations.
- Design doc lists fallback keyboard shortcuts and ARIA labels for peek overlay and cost-lens controls.

Constraints & tradeoffs: 
- Must avoid conflict with OS-level edge gestures (macOS Mission Control, Windows snap). We will scope an OS-compatibility matrix and disable edge-swipe where conflicts are irreconcilable.
- Cost-lens overlay must be read-optimized; we prioritize clarity of token cost and latency breakdown over full console telemetry in the peek.
- Progressive rollout recommended: start with 10% of internal staff via feature flag, collect telemetry and session recordings, then expand to customers as toggle.

Next steps: 
1) Share prototype with PM and ENG for technical feasibility (ENG-7112) — due 2026-03-16.
2) Run 6 formative usability sessions (research script attached) — sessions complete by 2026-03-18.
3) Finalize design spec and handoff package (Figma + confluence doc + telemetry table) — complete by 2026-03-20.

Notes: This approach targets power users (SREs, Platform Eng) who frequently flip between rollouts and cost dashboards and want a fast, context-preserving navigation pattern.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma prototype demonstrates edge-swipe peek and route scrub flows on desktop and tablet; 2) Usability score: >=80% task success across 6 participants; 3) Design spec lists telemetry events and keyboard fallbacks; 4) Engineering sign-off on non-conflicting gesture defaults and feature-flag rollout plan.
